quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. What should motorcyclists do?

options.text: Stay away from the oil and grease buildup.
Do not worry about the oil and grease buildup.
Find the lane with the least amount of oil and grease buildup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay away from the oil and grease buildup.
questions.explanation: Stay away from oil and grease buildup. The oily strip in the center of a lane is usually only about two feet wide. You can often ride to the left or right side of the oil and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle is more powerful?
questions.explanation: The front brake on a motorcycle is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What do service signs look like?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation is best for keeping riders together while leaving proper space between them?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of motorcyclists to stay close together while giving each rider enough space to ride safely.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To avoid a sudden power change in the middle of the turn
To keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid a sudden power change in the middle of the turn
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting gears while turning can suddenly change the power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Yes, they are required for all riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road
Follow closer to the vehicle ahead
Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: When riding at night, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Slow down and be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: What is the key to making a quick turn on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn or avoid an obstacle, make your motorcycle lean quickly in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: How many collisions between motorcycles and cars are caused by drivers not yielding the right-of-way to motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: More than half of collisions between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers of larger vehicles will yield, even if they are legally required to do so.

questions.question: When riding with a group of motorcyclists, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is generally good for group riding. However, switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A sign that your front tire has gone flat is that your steering suddenly feels:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a passenger vehicle's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is not as loud as car horns. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it for safety.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should attempt to avoid obstacles on the roadway. If avoiding an obstacle is not possible, the motorcyclist should:

options.text: Speed up before coming into contact with the object.
Stay seated so the seat can cushion some of the impact.
Try to approach the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to approach the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at close to a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should maintain a following distance of at least:
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second gap between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is best to:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks of cars ahead of you. The left tire track often works best, but adjust based on traffic.

questions.question: If you must transport a load, it should be:

options.text: Carried on the gas tank in front of you.
Piled up against a sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.

questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: You will get the most protection from a helmet if it is all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A helmet gives the best protection when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If you have a passenger aboard your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride at speeds that are slower than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how the motorcycle handles. Ride slower and allow extra stopping distance. The passenger should hold onto the handgrips or firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or midsection.

questions.question: A person with a minimum blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ is considered intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. No intoxicated person can operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: When making a regular stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Also downshift gears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a traffic law sign. It is white with red and black markings. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris collect in which part of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you:

options.text: Can go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You must pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. Your position should prevent other riders from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, pick a position where other drivers can see you best. Cover the clutch and both brakes to react faster. Slow down. Do not change speed or position suddenly as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: A motorized bicycle or moped cannot go faster than:
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized bicycle or moped is a two- or three-wheel vehicle that cannot go faster than 30 miles per hour on flat ground.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: In California, it is illegal for drivers under 21 to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, you must be 21 to drink alcohol. Drivers under 21 cannot operate any vehicle with a BAC of 0.01 percent or more. Riding a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol may be unsafe, even if under the legal limit.
